title: COMP/4/2015 of Doon Valley Colonisers And Builders p Ltd Vs The Registrar Of Companies Uttar Pradesh And Uttarakhand

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Company Petition No. 04 of 2015
Doon Valley Colonisers and
Builders (P) Ltd. ... Petitioner

versus
Registrar of Companies,
Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. ... Respondent
Mr. P.R. Mullick, Advocate for the petitioner company.
Mr. Lalit Sharma, Standing Counsel for Union of India/respondent.
U.C. Dhyani, J. (oral)

By means of this petition, the petitioner has challenged
the impugned order dated 31.07.2007, published in the
official Gazette on 22-28/03/2008 (copy Annexure 4 to the
writ petition) by which name of the petitioner's company has
been struck off and also for direction to the Registrar of
Companies to restore the name of the company on the roll of
the companies.
2. Briefly stated the facts giving rise to the above
company petition are that the petitioner is a private limited
company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956. The
petitioner company was duly registered and incorporated on
17.05.1988 bearing registration CIN No.
45201UR1988C009648. The petitioner company was
incorporated with the objective, inter alia, for doing the
business of Colonizers & Developers, to carry on the
business of purchase, sale, taken on lease, hire of acquire
land, factory, buildings, houses, shops and real estate etc. It
acquired 50 bighas (approx.) of land at Village, Tarla Nagal,
Parwa Doon, Dehradun during the period 1989-1991, with
two Directors namely, late T.R. Khurana and late Smt Satya

2
Khurana, leaving behind two married daughters Smt. Seema
Khurana and Mrs. Reema Khurana, who were employed
outside Dehradun. Presently, there are two Directors namely,
Pradeep Nagrath and Mrs. Reema Khurana. Lately, when the
Directors visited Dehradun they were informed by their
Chartered Accountant, after carrying search on the portal of
Registrar of Companies (respondent), that the company had
been declared a defunct company and the names had been
struck off by the Registrar of Companies. It was in active
operations till about 1996. The Directors had infused funds
by way of authorised share capital of Rs. 10,00,000/- and
48,000 shares of Rs. 10/- each had been issued. The company
did not file its balance sheets and annual returns as per the
requirements of Section 159 and 220 with the Registrar of
Company after 1996. Therefore, its name was struck off
under Section 560 by Registrar of Company.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner company submitted
that before striking off the name of the defaulting company,
the Registrar of Companies has to first issue a show cause
notice under Section 560(1) of the Companies Act, seeking
response of the defaulting company, showing reasons as to
why the returns are not being filed. Learned counsel for the
petitioner company vehemently argued that no such show
cause notice was ever issued to the petitioner company at its
registered office at Dehradun and / or to the Directors and, as
such, principles of natural justice and fair play were given a
go by and provisions of Section 560(2) of he Companies Act,
1956, were not complied with before striking off the name.

3
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner drew attention of this
Court to the Sub-Section (6) of Section 560 of the Companies
Act, which reads as under:-
"(6) If a company, or any member or creditor
thereof, feels aggrieved by the company having been
struck off the register, the Court, on an application
made by the company, member or creditor before the
expiry of twenty years from the publication in the
Official Gazette of the notice aforesaid, may, if
satisfied that the company was, at the time of the
striking off, carrying on business or in operation or
otherwise that it is just that the company be restored
to its register, order the name of the company to be
restored to the register, and the Court may, by the
order, give such directions and make such provisions
as seem just for placing the company and all other
persons in the same position as nearly as may be as
if the name of the company had not been struck off."
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner also submitted that
the Court otherwise has power, if it thinks just and proper
that the company be restored to the register, order the name
of the company to be restored to the register. He further
submitted that as per sub-section (6) of Section 560 of the
Act, the company or any shareholder (member) may apply
before the expiry of twenty years from the publication in the
Official Gazette of the notice, before the Court for restoration
of his name in company register, which is maintained by the
Registrar of Companies and also submitted that impugned
order has been passed in the year 2008, therefore, the
application moved on behalf of the petitioner is well within
time, i.e., before the expiry of twenty years.

4
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner company stated
before this Court that the company is still continuing its
business of colonizers, developers and real estate, as it is in
possession of about 50 bighas of land in Village Tarla Nagal,
Parwa Doon, Dehradun.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner in support of his
arguments, has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi
High Court, passed in Medtech Pharma (India) Private
Limited. Vs. Registrar of Companies, 2010 INDLAW DEL
1074, wherein the Delhi High Court has restored the name of
the company by following the judgment of various High
Courts. Para 10 of the said judgment is being reproduced as
under:-
"10. I might notice that Rule 94 of the Companies
(Court) Rules, 1959, states inter alia as follows;
Unless for any special reasons that the Court shall
otherwise order, the order shall direct that the
petitioners do pay to the Registrar of Companies his
costs of, and occasioned by the petition."
8. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and after
going through the judgment of Delhi High Court, cited above,
and in exercise of power under sub-section (6) of Section 5 of
the Companies Act, and after perusal of documents filed with
the petitions, it appears that the Company is still engaged in
its business, therefore, this Court is of the view that the name
of the Company be restored to the Register, under the name
of the Company with Registrar of Companies, subject to the
payment of cost amounting to Rs.25,000/-, to be deposited by
the company with the High Court Bar Association Welfare
Fund. In addition, further cost of Rs.25,000/- be paid to the

5
Bar Association, Dehradun. The cost be paid within a period
of one month from today.
9. The restoration of name of the petitioner company
would be subject to completion of all formalities including
payment of any late fee or any other charges, leviable by the
respondent for late deposit of statutory documents. The
impugned order dated 31.07.2007 and Publication in the
official gazette dated March 22 - March 28, 2008, stands set
aside. The name of the petitioner company, its Director, and
Members, as a consequence, shall stand restored to the
register of the Registrar of Companies, as the name of the
Company had not been struck off, in accordance with Section
560(6) of the Companies Act, 1956.
10. Petitioner is also directed to file a certified copy of its
returns before the Registrar for compliance of the Court's
order and shall also present the receipt of the cost before the
Registrar. If said cost of Rs.50,000/- is not paid within a
period of one month, as directed above, the impugned order
shall automatically stand recalled.
11. This disposes of the company petition.
12. Stay application no. 13672 of 2015 also stands
disposed of.
(U.C. Dhyani, J.)
